articles.title: Optimizely Breach Put Wallet-Swapping Code on 178 Sites, Including Ledger
articles.excerpt: The injected script swapped crypto addresses on pages from HSBC, Ledger, Zoom and others on Nov. 16. Wallets tied to it took in about $7,040, Report URI said.
articles.body_md:
An attacker slipped crypto-stealing code into websites run by 178 organizations on Monday, Nov. 16, through a flaw in Optimizely's web-testing service. The affected sites included hardware wallet maker Ledger, HSBC, Zoom, the BBC and CNN, according to security researcher Scott Helme of Report URI, as summarized by [StepSecurity](https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/optimjack-optimizely-hosted-scripts-crypto-clipper-card-skimmer) and [The Hacker News](https://thehackernews.com/2026/11/hijacked-optimizely-scripts-served-card.html).

Optimizely said an unauthorized party exploited a vulnerability in its Experimentation product and added malicious JavaScript to some customer projects, [StepSecurity](https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/optimjack-optimizely-hosted-scripts-crypto-clipper-card-skimmer) reported, citing the company's status page. Optimizely said it fixed the flaw, removed the code and secured affected accounts.

### How the script stole crypto

Many sites load small scripts from outside vendors to run tests and track visitors. Here, the attacker wrote code into a custom field in each Optimizely project, so it rode along on every page of every affected site without touching the sites' own servers.

The script looked for crypto addresses on eight networks, including Bitcoin, Ethereum, Solana and Tron. When it found one near a word like "wallet," "deposit" or "send," it swapped in the attacker's address, including in text a visitor copied to the clipboard. Because the replacement passed the chain's checksum, a wallet app would accept it. It also tried to skim card numbers typed into checkout forms and loaded exploit kits aimed at iPhones, [BleepingComputer](https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/optimizely-supply-chain-attack-infects-major-brands-sites-with-malware/) and StepSecurity said.

Helme found the code in 188 of the 1,611 Optimizely snippets he checked, and said the real count is likely higher. Six of the organizations are crypto or trading firms and 32 are banks or financial companies.

Wallets hard-coded in the script had received about $7,040 within roughly nine hours, Report URI estimated, per [The Hacker News](https://thehackernews.com/2026/11/hijacked-optimizely-scripts-served-card.html). StepSecurity put the total near $6,600 and noted that two addresses were in use before the attack, so not every transfer can be tied to a victim. It said the attacker emptied the bitcoin, ether and litecoin wallets early Tuesday, UTC.

Ledger and HSBC had not commented in the reports reviewed by Black Mint as of 5:50 a.m. ET.

*In our opinion: The dollar figure is small. The reach is not, because one vendor account pushed code to 178 brands at once. Anyone who copied a deposit address from an affected site on Nov. 16 should compare it character by character with the address shown in their own wallet or exchange account before sending again.*

articles.title: Wells Fargo Reports $2.35 Billion in BlackRock's Bitcoin ETF, Up From $812 Million
articles.excerpt: Wells Fargo's 13F shows 49.58 million IBIT shares on Sept. 30, about double June's count. The filing includes client accounts, not just the bank's own money.
articles.body_md:
Wells Fargo reported 49.58 million shares of BlackRock's iShares Bitcoin Trust (IBIT) worth $2.35 billion at the end of September, up from 24.40 million shares worth $812 million three months earlier, according to its [quarterly 13F filing](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/72971/000007297126000342/13F_9_2026.xml) made Monday, Nov. 16. The share count roughly doubled. The dollar value nearly tripled.

The gap between those two numbers is mostly price. Bitcoin rose about 42% from June 30 to Sept. 30, based on BlackRock's figures, [CoinDesk](https://www.coindesk.com/markets/2026/11/17/wells-fargo-s-reported-blackrock-bitcoin-etf-holdings-double-to-usd2-35-billion) reported. The same filing also lists options on IBIT: calls covering 717,200 shares and puts covering 540,000 shares.

### What a 13F does and doesn't show

A 13F is a snapshot that large investment managers file with the SEC 45 days after each quarter ends, listing the U.S.-traded stocks and funds they oversee. Wells Fargo's filing covers the bank and several of its investment managers, and many of the positions sit in accounts run for clients. So it tells readers how much IBIT runs through the Wells Fargo system, not how much bitcoin exposure the bank carries on its own balance sheet. The [June-quarter filing](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/72971/000007297126000304/13F_6_2026.xml) gives the earlier figures.

CoinDesk estimated the position equals about 28,070 bitcoin, based on IBIT holding 801,033 BTC against 1.415 billion shares on Sept. 30.

The numbers are seven weeks old. Bitcoin traded at $64,212 at 5:52 a.m. ET Tuesday, according to [CoinGecko](https://www.coingecko.com/en/coins/bitcoin), down 0.4% in 24 hours. The filing says nothing about whether those accounts bought or sold since.

*In our opinion: The more telling detail is the 103% jump in share count. Price alone can't explain that, so the bank's advisers and clients were adding IBIT through the summer. The next real check is the December-quarter 13F, due in mid-February, which will show what they did during the slide.*

articles.title: CFTC Approves Backpack's U.S. Exchange and Clearinghouse for Crypto Perps
articles.excerpt: The CFTC designated Backpack's exchange on Nov. 16, three days after registering its clearinghouse. No U.S. launch date has been set.
articles.body_md:
The Commodity Futures Trading Commission approved Backpack's U.S. derivatives exchange on Monday, Nov. 16, three days after it registered the firm's clearinghouse. That gives the crypto company both federal licenses it needs to offer leveraged perpetual futures to American traders. It has not said when trading starts.

The agency designated TLD Markets, Inc., which does business as Backpack Exchange, as a contract market in an [order of designation](https://www.cftc.gov/filings/documents/2026/orgdcmtldbackpackord261116.pdf) dated Nov. 16. Its affiliate, TLD Clearing, Inc., or Backpack Clearing, was registered on Nov. 13 to clear margined futures and fully collateralized futures, options on futures and swaps, the [CFTC's clearinghouse registry](https://www.cftc.gov/IndustryOversight/IndustryFilings/ClearingOrganizations) shows.

### Two licenses, two jobs

A designated contract market is a federally supervised exchange that can list futures and options. A derivatives clearing organization is the clearinghouse behind it: it stands between buyer and seller on each trade, collects margin and guarantees settlement if one side can't pay. Perpetual futures, the product Backpack plans to list, are futures with no expiry date, so a trader can hold a leveraged position open as long as margin holds up.

Backpack said in a [press release](https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2026/11/16/3404185/0/en/backpack-receives-landmark-cftc-approval-to-establish-first-ever-blockchain-based-derivatives-exchange-in-the-united-states-with-global-unified-liquidity.html) that U.S. users will be able to trade those contracts 24/7, post cash or crypto as collateral, cross-margin positions and trade in the same global order book as its overseas customers. The company called it the first blockchain-based derivatives exchange in the U.S. and said it serves users in more than 150 countries and regions, with more than $450 billion in trading volume. [The Defiant](https://thedefiant.io/news/regulation/cftc-approves-backpack-s-blockchain-derivatives-venue) reported the U.S. service is still taking waitlist sign-ups.

"From a policy perspective this is a really big deal," said Mark Wetjen, president of Backpack US, adding that it moves "price discovery from offshore unregulated venues to the United States."

CFTC Chairman Michael Selig said in a [statement](https://www.cftc.gov/PressRoom/SpeechesTestimony/seligstatement111626) that the law sets core principles "without prescribing a particular technological architecture." He added that firms built on blockchains must meet the same standards as everyone else, including anti-money laundering programs, segregation of customer funds, market surveillance and system safeguards.

*In our opinion: Backpack's pitch is that leveraged crypto trading belongs onshore, under a U.S. regulator's rules on margin and customer money. It now holds both licenses to test that idea. The paperwork is done, but the order book is still a waitlist, so the launch date and how much volume shows up are the numbers to watch.*

articles.title: New Zealand Forecasters Lift One-Year Inflation Outlook to 2.92%
articles.excerpt: One-year expectations jumped 32 basis points in the RBNZ survey, while five- and 10-year views eased. Forecasters see the cash rate at 3.40% in a year.
articles.body_md:
New Zealand's business leaders and professional forecasters now expect inflation of 2.92% a year from now, up from 2.60% three months ago, the Reserve Bank of New Zealand's [Survey of Expectations](https://www.rbnz.govt.nz/-/media/project/sites/rbnz/files/statistics/series/m/m14/insights/2026/survey-of-expectations-november-2026.pdf) showed on Tuesday, Nov. 17, local time. That is a 32-basis-point jump in one quarter.

The longer view moved the other way. Two-year expectations edged up to 2.36% from 2.34%, five-year expectations fell to 2.17% from 2.31%, and 10-year expectations slipped to 2.13% from 2.20%, according to the survey and [Trading Economics](https://tradingeconomics.com/new-zealand/inflation-expectations/news/601736).

### What the survey measures

Every quarter the central bank asks a panel of executives and economists where they think prices, wages and interest rates are heading. This round drew 44 responses, collected from Oct. 23 to 30. The two-year figure gets the most attention because that is roughly when a rate change made today works its way into prices, [FXStreet](https://www.fxstreet.com/news/rbnz-survey-nz-two-year-inflation-expectations-rise-to-236-qoq-in-q4-2026-202611170203) noted. Expectations matter on their own, too: a firm that expects higher costs tends to raise prices and wages in advance.

Respondents also lifted their rate forecast. They see the Official Cash Rate at 3.40% a year from now, up from 3.21% in the last survey, and at 3.05% by the end of December. Actual inflation was 3.7% in the September quarter, down from 4.1% in June, and unemployment rose to 5.7%, the RBNZ said.

For markets, the survey adds New Zealand to a list of places where rate expectations are climbing. Kansas City Fed President Jeffrey Schmid said on Sunday the Fed "has some work to do on inflation," [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/15/fed-has-some-work-to-do-on-inflation-kansas-city-fed-chief-says.html) reported. Higher expected rates raise the return on cash and bonds, which compete for the same money as assets with no yield, such as bitcoin.

*In our opinion: The split is the real story. Forecasters see a bumpier year ahead but still trust the long run, with 10-year expectations at 2.13%, close to the RBNZ's 2% target midpoint. Borrowers carry the stake, since the one-year cash-rate forecast rose 19 basis points in a single survey. The next check is the central bank's own rate decision and whether it sounds as worried as its panel.*

articles.title: Strategy's Debt and Preferred Stock Cost $1.43 Billion a Year
articles.excerpt: Its 850,849 bitcoin cost $75,452 each, above Monday's price. A $4.75 billion cash reserve covers about 40 months of interest and dividends.
articles.body_md:
Strategy needs about $1.43 billion a year to cover interest on its convertible notes and dividends on five preferred stocks, its [Nov. 15 investor briefing](https://assets.contentstack.io/v3/assets/bltf8d808d9b8cebd37/blt36fbde4f9ee6bd70/6afa7fcf5a0d255dea73ad18/MSTR_Investor_Briefing_As_of_2026-11-15.pdf) shows. Its 850,849 bitcoin sat below cost Monday.

**How the borrowing works**

A convertible note is a loan the lender can swap for stock at a set price, so it carries a low coupon. Perpetual preferred stock never matures. It pays a fixed dividend ahead of common shareholders, and if it's "cumulative," a skipped payment piles up and must be paid before common holders get anything.

**850,849 coins bought over six years**

The company paid $64.20 billion for its coins, or $75,452 each including fees, its [Nov. 16 8-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1050446/0001193125-26-462151.txt) shows. It held 70,469 at the end of 2020 and 447,470 at the end of 2024, earlier filings show. With bitcoin at $64,922 at 3:42 p.m. ET Monday, per [CoinGecko](https://www.coingecko.com/en/coins/bitcoin), the stack was worth about $55.2 billion, roughly $9 billion under cost. That loss stays on paper unless coins are sold.

**$6.71 billion of notes, mostly at 0%**

Six series were outstanding on Sept. 30, the [quarterly filing](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1050446/000105044626000060/mstr-20260930.htm) shows. Each lets holders demand cash on a put date:

- $1.01 billion at 0.625%, due 2028, put Sept. 15, 2027, converts at $183.19
- $1.5 billion at 0%, due 2029, put June 1, 2028, converts at $672.40
- $2 billion at 0%, due 2030, put March 1, 2028, converts at $433.43
- $800 million at 0.625%, due 2030, put Sept. 15, 2028, converts at $149.77
- $603.7 million at 0.875%, due 2031, put Sept. 15, 2028, converts at $232.72
- $800 million at 2.25%, due 2032, put June 15, 2029, converts at $204.33

Coupons cost about $34.6 million a year. MSTR traded near $103.32 at 3:43 p.m. ET, per Yahoo Finance, below every conversion price.

**The preferred bill is the big one**

Rates are from the 10-Q; the STRC count subtracts weekly buybacks since Oct. 25:

- STRC: 12%, cumulative, paid daily; about 77.6 million shares, roughly $932 million a year
- STRD: 10%, not cumulative; $140.2 million
- STRF: 10%, cumulative; $128.4 million
- STRK: 8%, cumulative, payable in cash or stock; $112.2 million
- STRE: 10% in euros, cumulative; €77.5 million, about $85 million

With coupons, that's about $1.43 billion, matching Strategy's figure.

**Where the money comes from**

Software won't cover it. Third-quarter revenue was $125.4 million, and the 10-Q says software cash isn't expected to meet the company's needs.

The USD Reserve held $4.75 billion on Nov. 15, plus $151.2 million of USD Cash, the 8-K says. Board policy keeps at least 12 months of payments in it. At $1.43 billion a year, the reserve alone covers about 40 months. Strategy puts both pools at 3.42 years.

New stock fills the rest. Strategy sold $244.7 million of MSTR shares last week and has $18.09 billion of sales capacity left.

It has also sold bitcoin: about 6,947 coins this year for $431.8 million, to fund dividends and STRC buybacks, the 10-Q and its [Oct. 29 earnings release](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1050446/000105044626000047/mstr-20261029x8kxex9912.htm) show.

**mNAV and a falling bitcoin**

mNAV is Strategy's share price divided by its bitcoin per share after debt and preferred claims, net of cash. It was 1.09x at Nov. 13 prices, the briefing and [strategy.com](https://www.strategy.com/) show. Our recalculation at Monday afternoon prices gives about 1.1x.

Near or below 1x, new MSTR sales add less per share. The briefing warns that issuance "below appropriate value can reduce Net BPS." A deeper bitcoin slide thins the cushion behind the preferred. STRC traded as low as about $71 in June, the 10-Q says.

**Rates set the price of money**

The Federal Reserve held its target range at 3.75% to 4% on Oct. 28, [its statement](https://www.federalreserve.gov/newsevents/pressreleases/monetary20261028a.htm) shows, and meets again Dec. 8-9. STRC pays about eight points over that. Interest on Strategy's cash paid for $21.8 million of last week's STRC buybacks. Rate cuts would shrink that income.

*In our opinion: the yearly bill looks covered for now, with about 40 months of reserve and no new stock sold. The harder stretch starts in September 2027, when holders can demand cash for $1.01 billion of notes, then $4.9 billion more in 2028. Every series converts above Monday's share price. The number to check each Monday is mNAV in the 8-K and on strategy.com, since it decides whether new stock or bitcoin sales pay the bill.*

articles.title: Judge Acquits Peraire-Bueno Brothers in $25 Million Ethereum MEV Case
articles.excerpt: A year after a jury deadlocked, Judge Jessica Clarke ruled prosecutors showed no material misrepresentation, so wire fraud convictions couldn't stand.
articles.body_md:
A federal judge in Manhattan on Monday acquitted Anton and James Peraire-Bueno, the MIT-educated brothers charged over $25 million in crypto taken from Ethereum trading bots in about 12 seconds in April 2023.

U.S. District Judge Jessica Clarke granted the brothers' motion for acquittal. She found prosecutors had not shown at trial that the pair made any material misrepresentation, which wire fraud requires, [Reuters reported](https://www.jpost.com/international/article-915104). [Bloomberg Law](https://news.bloomberglaw.com/business-and-practice/mit-brothers-acquitted-in-25-million-crypto-case-avoid-retrial) reported the ruling means the brothers avoid a retrial. A jury deadlocked on every count in November 2025, and Clarke declared a mistrial then.

"The question before the court is not whether the Peraire-Buenos' conduct was right or moral, or even whether it violated uncharged crimes," Clarke wrote, according to Reuters. She added that the transactions "were not placed on a regulated market with rules prohibiting this conduct."

**How the trade worked**

MEV, or maximal extractable value, is the extra profit available from choosing which transactions go into a block and in what order, per [ethereum.org](https://ethereum.org/en/developers/docs/mev/). Automated "sandwich" bots chase it by trading just before and just after another user's trade.

Prosecutors said the brothers used bait transactions to lure those bots, then exploited a flaw in MEV-Boost, software most Ethereum validators run to receive blocks from outside builders, to swap in their own transactions and drain the bots. The defense argued it was a legitimate trading strategy. The brothers were indicted in May 2024, and Reuters said no scheme of this type had been federally prosecuted before.

A spokesperson for U.S. Attorney James McDonald's office declined to comment, and the brothers' lawyers had no immediate comment, Reuters said.

*In our opinion: the ruling is narrow. Clarke tested the case against wire fraud only, and her own words leave room for "uncharged crimes." For MEV searchers and the validators they pay, the open question is where code-exploiting trades sit in U.S. law. On this record, wire fraud wasn't the answer.*

articles.title: Nasdaq Drops 2.5% as Nvidia Slide Drags Tech, Bitcoin Holds Near $65,400
articles.excerpt: Nvidia fell 4.1% to $156.14 ahead of Tuesday's earnings, and the S&P 500 lost 1.9% for a third straight drop. Bitcoin was up 0.4% over 24 hours.
articles.body_md:
The Nasdaq Composite fell 2.49% on Monday to 24,509.76, its third straight loss, as Nvidia led another sell-off in chip and AI stocks.

The S&P 500 lost 1.92% to 7,416.59 and the Dow fell 739.38 points, or 1.41%, to 51,608.17, per [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/15/stock-market-today-live-updates.html) and [AP](https://apnews.com/article/stocks-markets-ai-nvidia-oil-us-35786b8f539ec95f16ae0500f71cfcc7). Bitcoin went the other way, barely. It sat at $65,429 at 5:47 p.m. ET, up 0.4% over 24 hours, per CoinGecko. Ether was at $1,832, up 0.3%.

**Nvidia's slide since October**

Nvidia closed at $156.14, down 4.12%, [Investing.com](https://www.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/us-stocks-lower-at-close-of-trade-dow-jones-industrial-average-down-141-5030993) data show. That is about 35% below its record close of $239.24 on Oct. 6, [The Washington Post](https://www.washingtonpost.com/business/2026/11/16/stock-market-drops-amid-continued-nvidia-fallout/) reported. Jensen Huang resigned as CEO last week. The company reports third-quarter results after Tuesday's close.

The selling spread. Micron fell 7.62% and Intel 7.07%, and Morgan Stanley, Goldman Sachs and JPMorgan each lost more than 2%, per CNBC. Falling stocks beat rising ones on the NYSE by 2,197 to 655.

**Why chip stocks matter to crypto**

Nvidia sits at the center of what traders call the AI trade, and CNBC said Tuesday's results will be judged as much on how the company moves forward after Huang's exit as on the numbers. Crypto feels it through the same pool of investors: a sell-off that cuts tech portfolios can leave less appetite for other volatile assets. On Monday, that spillover didn't show up in bitcoin's price.

Bitcoin had already taken its hit. It fell to about $62,000 late Saturday, its lowest since August, after forced selling of leveraged bets, [CNBC reported](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/16/bitcoin-slides-to-62000-following-liquidation-cascade-then-rebounds-slightly.html). The Crypto Fear & Greed Index read 10, or "Extreme Fear," on Monday.

*In our opinion: on a 2.5% down day for the Nasdaq, bitcoin was the calm one in the room while chip stocks took the losses. That split lasted one session, with a Fear & Greed reading of 10 behind it. The bigger test is Tuesday night, when Nvidia's numbers land with a new leadership story attached. The number to watch is bitcoin's Saturday low near $62,000, and whether Monday's split survives Wednesday's open.*

articles.title: Four Democratic Senators Press SEC on Tokenized Stock Exemption's AML Gaps
articles.excerpt: The senators asked SEC Chair Paul Atkins how know-your-customer rules apply when tokenized shares move to unverified wallets. The SEC declined to comment.
articles.body_md:
Four Democratic senators asked SEC Chair Paul Atkins on Monday to explain how anti-money-laundering rules apply under the agency's five-year exemption for tokenized stock trading, [The Block](https://www.theblock.co/news/regulation/2026-11-16-democratic-senators-warn-secs-tokenized-stock-exemption-illicit-finance-gaps-441432) and [TokenPost](https://www.tokenpost.com/news/regulation/58817) reported.

Sens. Angela Alsobrooks, Ruben Gallego, Mark Warner and Catherine Cortez Masto signed the letter.

**What the exemption allows**

A tokenized stock is a blockchain token that represents a share of a company. It can move between wallets. The SEC's innovation exemption, launched in September, lets qualifying "tokenized securities venues" trade these tokens for up to five years without registering as a national securities exchange, both outlets reported.

Know-your-customer (KYC) and anti-money-laundering (AML) rules require platforms to verify who their customers are and watch for suspicious money. The senators said the exemption doesn't spell out how those checks apply to trades, or whether a venue must limit who can receive a token. Their concern: a buyer who passed identity checks could send the token to an unverified wallet, including one held by a foreign person or someone engaged in illegal activity, outside U.S. oversight.

**Pricing, opt-outs and rulemaking**

The letter also raised retail pricing protections and said companies should be able to opt out of having their stock tokenized. The senators asked how the SEC will enforce AML standards and check platforms' disclosures and self-verification, and they asked that any further changes come through a formal, public rulemaking.

Formal rulemaking means the SEC would publish a proposal and take public comment before a rule is final, unlike an exemption the agency can grant on its own.

The SEC declined to comment on the letter, The Block said.

articles.title: Strategy Buys 485 Bitcoin as Its Stack Sits $9 Billion Below Cost
articles.excerpt: The 485 coins cost $33.4 million. Strategy also sold $244.7 million of stock, and most of that cash went to buying back its STRC preferred shares.
articles.body_md:
Strategy bought 485 bitcoin for $33.4 million last week, its 8-K filing shows, while its full 850,849-coin holding sat about $9.3 billion below what the company paid for it.

The company's average cost is $75,452 per coin, or $64.20 billion in total, as of Nov. 15. With bitcoin near $64,550 at 11:45 a.m. ET Monday, per CoinGecko, the stack was worth about $54.9 billion. That gap is on paper. It becomes a realized loss only if Strategy sells.

**Most of the new cash went to preferred stock**

Strategy sold 2,087,040 shares of its MSTR common stock between Nov. 9 and Nov. 15 through an at-the-market program, raising $244.7 million after commissions. Only $33.4 million of it bought bitcoin, at an average of $68,887 each. Another $206.3 million went to repurchasing its STRC preferred stock, and $5 million went to cash, the filing says.

An at-the-market program lets a company sell new shares into the market a little at a time, at current prices, instead of in one large offering. STRC is Strategy's variable-rate perpetual preferred stock: it pays holders a dividend and has no maturity date. Buying it back cuts the number of those shares outstanding.

**Bitcoin's slide sets the backdrop**

Bitcoin fell as low as about $62,000 late Saturday, its lowest since August, per Coin Metrics data cited by [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/16/bitcoin-slides-to-62000-following-liquidation-cascade-then-rebounds-slightly.html). CoinGecko's hourly data puts the Saturday low near $62,600 at 9 p.m. ET. CNBC tied the drop to forced selling of leveraged bets and a stronger dollar. Bitcoin is down about 14% from $75,270 a week earlier, per CoinGecko.

Strategy wasn't the only treasury company buying. Bitmine Immersion said Monday it added 7,653 ether last week and now holds 6,077,745 ETH.

*In our opinion: the share sale tells the real story. Of every dollar Strategy raised last week, roughly 14 cents went to bitcoin and about 84 cents went to buying back its own preferred stock. Next Monday's 8-K will show whether that mix holds while the stack trades below cost.*

articles.title: Supreme Court Rejects Custodia's Bid for a Fed Master Account
articles.excerpt: The justices gave no reason and noted no dissent, leaving in place a 2-1 appeals ruling that lets regional Fed banks turn down eligible banks.
articles.body_md:
The U.S. Supreme Court on Monday declined to hear Custodia Bank's appeal, ending the Wyoming crypto bank's fight for a Federal Reserve master account that began with its October 2020 application.

The justices gave no explanation, and no dissent was recorded, [Quartz reported](https://qz.com/custodia-bank-supreme-court-fed-master-account-111626), citing Bloomberg. The order leaves standing an Oct. 31, 2025, ruling by the 10th Circuit Court of Appeals, which held 2-1 that the Federal Reserve Bank of Kansas City had discretion to reject Custodia's application. The Supreme Court did not rule on the merits, and the denial ends the case.

**What a master account does**

A master account is a bank's own account at a regional Fed bank. It lets the bank settle payments directly with the Fed and use systems such as Fedwire, which moves large dollar transfers between banks. A bank without one has to route money through a correspondent bank, a larger bank that holds funds and moves them on its behalf.

Custodia applied under a Wyoming special purpose depository institution charter, which lets it offer digital-asset custody. The Kansas City Fed denied the application in January 2023, citing the bank's concentration in crypto-related activities. A federal trial court in Wyoming sided with the Fed in March 2024.

**Both sides' arguments**

Custodia argued that federal law entitles eligible banks to have their applications approved. "Congress did not intend for access to the nation's banking system to depend on unaccountable regional Fed banks' whim," the bank told the court, Quartz reported, citing Bloomberg. The Trump administration urged the justices not to take the case, arguing the Federal Reserve Act gives reserve banks discretion. Black Mint found no public statement from Custodia on Monday's order as of noon ET.

The Fed has proposed a narrower "payment account" that would pay no interest and give no access to Fed credit. Kraken's banking unit received a limited purpose account from the Kansas City Fed in March, [Crypto Briefing reported](https://cryptobriefing.com/supreme-court-rejects-custodia-fed-master-account/). Custodia told the court that kind of account would not be enough.

*In our opinion: the decision that counts now is the Fed's own. Comments on its payment-account proposal closed July 27, and the final version will set how much of the payment system crypto-focused banks can reach without a master account. Custodia's own timeline is the measure of the court route: six years from application to Monday's order.*

articles.title: Solana Retires Its 'Mainnet Beta' Label After Six Years Live
articles.excerpt: Solana 1.0 is now a shared protocol version that both the Agave and Firedancer clients can point to. SOL holders don't need to do anything.
articles.body_md:
Solana is officially out of beta. The Solana Foundation on Monday retired the "mainnet beta" label the network has carried since its March 2020 launch and introduced Solana 1.0, a version number for the network's rules.

Nothing changes for SOL holders. The foundation said balances, accounts, apps and transaction history stay the same, and users don't need to swap tokens or install anything. The rename doesn't make transactions faster or cheaper on its own.

**One number for two clients**

A blockchain protocol is the set of rules every validator follows, and a client is the software that runs those rules. Solana now has two major clients. Agave is built by Anza. Firedancer, built separately by Jump Crypto, went live on mainnet in December 2025. Each has its own code, release schedule and version numbers.

That made it hard to say which network rules a given release supported. "A shared protocol version lets everyone refer to Solana's evolution without using one client's release number as shorthand for the entire network," the foundation wrote, as quoted by [Solana Compass](https://solanacompass.com/news/solana-drops-the-mainnet-beta-label-and-introduces-solana-10-a-protocol-version-shared-by-agave-and-firedancer). Anza, the Agave team, confirmed that Agave keeps its own version numbers, Solana Compass reported.

**Operators still have homework**

The foundation said a protocol version "does not activate every associated improvement at once." Validator and RPC operators still need to check which client releases support each rollout and follow the activation steps in the Agave or Firedancer docs. The foundation's cluster page now lists the public endpoint as api.mainnet.solana.com, while Anza's docs still showed the mainnet-beta address on Monday, Solana Compass reported. Apps with a hard-coded "mainnet-beta" string are the ones to check against the Solana Changelog.

The rename follows Alpenglow, a consensus upgrade that went live Oct. 21 and targets finality of about 150 milliseconds, down from 12.8 seconds. Finality is the point where a transaction can't be reversed. SOL traded near $70.89 at 11:45 a.m. ET, down 0.8% in 24 hours, per CoinGecko.

*In our opinion: six years and eight months is a long beta for a network that settled real money from day one, so the label was about the last thing on Solana still in testing. The useful change is the shared number, because two clients on separate version schemes need a common reference before the next upgrade. The foundation hasn't said what the next protocol version will contain or when, and that schedule is the thing to watch.*

articles.title: Canada's Inflation Holds at 3.1% as Gasoline Prices Run 30.9% Higher
articles.excerpt: Economists polled by Reuters expected 3.2%. The Bank of Canada's preferred core gauges stayed near 2% ahead of its Dec. 9 rate decision.
articles.body_md:
Canada's annual inflation rate held at 3.1% in October, the same as September, Statistics Canada said Monday. Economists polled by Reuters had expected 3.2%. Prices rose 0.2% from September, against a forecast of 0.3%.

The reading lands three weeks before the Bank of Canada's Dec. 9 decision. The bank raised its overnight rate a quarter point to 2.50% on Oct. 28. After the release, traders priced roughly even odds of another hike in December, [the Globe and Mail reported](https://www.theglobeandmail.com/investing/markets/inside-the-market/article-how-todays-inflation-data-has-moved-markets-and-bets-for-future-boc/), citing swaps data from Bloomberg.

**Gasoline did most of the lifting**

Gasoline cost 30.9% more than a year earlier, up from 27.8% in September. StatCan said part of that is a base-year effect: gasoline fell 4.8% in October 2025, and that drop no longer counts in the 12-month figure. From September to October, gasoline fell 2.5%. Excluding energy, prices rose 2.0%, down from 2.1%.

The Bank of Canada aims for 2% inflation inside a 1% to 3% band, and it leans on "core" measures that strip out the most volatile prices. Its preferred gauges, CPI-trim and CPI-median, came in at 1.8% and 2.0%. So headline inflation sits above the band while the underlying measures sit near the target.

**Banks split on December**

CIBC senior economist Andrew Grantham said the report backs CIBC's call for a hold, [Canadian Mortgage Professional reported](https://www.mpamag.com/ca/mortgage-industry/industry-trends/october-inflation-steady-complicating-bocs-december-call/597526). RBC's Abbey Xu kept a base case of a quarter-point hike to 2.75%.

Rate moves reach crypto through yields and the dollar. Higher rates raise the return on cash and bonds, which compete with assets like bitcoin that pay no interest. Bitcoin was near $64,550 at 11:45 a.m. ET, down 0.2% over 24 hours, per CoinGecko.

The Bank of Canada announces its next decision on Dec. 9.

articles.title: DBS and JPMorgan Link Tokenized Dollars for 24/7 US-Singapore Moves
articles.excerpt: Ant International is the first client. Transfers into and out of JPMorgan's blockchain accounts still pause for three hours every Saturday.
articles.body_md:
DBS Bank and JPMorgan's Kinexys unit launched a service on Monday that lets institutional clients move tokenized U.S. dollars between Singapore and the U.S. 24 hours a day, seven days a week. Ant International is the first client.

For a corporate treasurer, that means cash sitting in Singapore can reach a U.S. subsidiary after the usual bank cut-off times instead of waiting for Monday morning.

**A bank deposit wearing a token**

A tokenized deposit is an ordinary bank balance recorded as a token on the bank's own blockchain. It is still a dollar claim on DBS or JPMorgan, not a new cryptocurrency. Both networks are permissioned, so only approved banks and clients can use them, unlike Bitcoin or Ethereum, where anyone can join.

The link joins DBS Token Services with Kinexys's Blockchain Deposit Account network. Partior, a settlement company both banks helped found, coordinates settlement, the [DBS release](https://www.dbs.com/newsroom/DBS_and_Kinexys_by_JP_Morgan_launch_industry_first_247_interoperability_solution_for_cross_border_tokenised_deposit_transfers) says. It puts into use a framework the two banks announced in November 2025, and DBS calls the setup "industry-first."

"Tokenised money is moving rapidly from experimentation to delivering live tangible value for clients," said Rachel Chew, DBS's chief operating officer and co-head of digital assets for global transaction services.

**The asterisk on "24/7"**

Transfers inside the Kinexys network run around the clock. Moving money between a traditional JPMorgan account and a blockchain account still stops from 3 p.m. to 6 p.m. ET each Saturday. The release says a fix is in development.

**What the banks left out**

The announcement gives no fees, transfer limits or dollar volumes so far. To size the opportunity, the banks cite a Money20/20 and FXC Intelligence forecast that Asia's outbound cross-border payments will grow from $13.5 trillion in 2025 to $24 trillion by 2033. In September, DBS and Citi reported a weekend dollar payment between the same two countries using tokenized deposits over Swift's Digital Ledger, [The Business Times](https://www.businesstimes.com.sg/companies-markets/dbs-jpmorgan-launch-us-singapore-tokenised-deposit-service-institutions) noted.

*In our opinion: the prize here is corporate cash that used to sit still from Friday night to Monday morning, and Ant International has signed up first. The next number to look for is client two, along with any fee schedule. Until that Saturday pause goes away, the old banking calendar still gets three hours a week.*

articles.title: Buterin Backs leanPCS as Faster Route to Quantum-Safe Ethereum
articles.excerpt: Quantum-safe signatures can run 1 to 6 kilobytes against 65 bytes today. EIP-8288 would fold them into one proof per block, but it is still a draft.
articles.body_md:
Vitalik Buterin said early Monday that he now backs a "leanPCS" version of EIP-8288, a draft Ethereum proposal meant to stop quantum-safe signatures, up to about 6 kilobytes each, from crowding blocks. Today's signatures take 65 bytes.

"Over the past few weeks I've gone from thinking leanPCS is total bull to being a total bull," the Ethereum co-founder [wrote on X](https://x.com/VitalikButerin/status/2122233780371083553) at 2:42 a.m. ET.

Bigger data takes more of Ethereum's limited block space, which can push fees up. Signatures and proofs built to resist quantum computers are much bigger. The [EIP text](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-8288) puts hash-based signatures at about 2 to 3 kB and 150,000 to 200,000 gas to verify, and STARK proofs at over 128 kB.

**How the bundling works**

A user still creates the large signature or proof and broadcasts it. Nodes holding pending transactions (the mempool) check what they have seen and, once per second under the draft, roll it into a single STARK, a hash-based proof that a list of checks passed. Those proofs get merged again until a block carries one "recursive STARK" in its header. The chain then stores short claims, about 64 to 96 bytes each by Buterin's count, instead of every signature.

**Three options on the table**

leanSPHINCS covers one hash-based signature type and nothing else. leanSTARK lets users prove any program, but developers would first have to agree on the instruction set those programs use; Buterin called that "a really big deal" because it would be hard to upgrade. leanPCS standardizes only a polynomial commitment scheme, the hardest part of a STARK. Buterin wrote that it could be built "very quickly" and that leanSTARK could follow later, though leanPCS is less efficient onchain.

**Draft only, no date**

The EIP, by Buterin and Thomas Coratger, was created June 3. Its reference implementation is listed as "TBD," and it would need a network upgrade. The published spec defines leanSPHINCS and leanSTARK modes. It does not yet describe a leanPCS mode.

articles.title: India's Wholesale Inflation Hits 12.29% as Fuel Prices Jump 32.8%
articles.excerpt: Crude oil and natural gas prices were up 70.8% from a year earlier. Economists in a Reuters poll had expected 12.1% for the headline rate.
articles.body_md:
India's wholesale prices rose 12.29% in October from a year earlier, up from 11.39% in September, the Ministry of Commerce and Industry said Monday. Economists in a [Reuters poll](https://www.thehindubusinessline.com/economy/indias-wholesale-price-rise-accelerates-to-1229-in-october/article71707029.ece) had expected 12.1%.

Energy did most of the work. Fuel and power inflation climbed to 32.84% from 25.85%, and crude petroleum and natural gas prices were up 70.80% on the year, the ministry's figures show. Fuel and power made up roughly nine-tenths of the index's 0.71% monthly rise, [Moneycontrol](https://www.moneycontrol.com/news/business/economy/wholesale-inflation-rises-to-12-29-in-october-as-fuel-and-power-prices-surge-14081055.html) calculated.

**What the wholesale index measures**

The Wholesale Price Index tracks what businesses pay for goods in bulk, before retail markups, so fuel and metal costs show up there first. It is a year-on-year measure. Last October the index was falling, at minus 1.18%, [Mint reported](https://www.livemint.com/economy/wpi-inflation-october-retail-inflation-food-prices-crude-oil-rbi-rate-hike-11794821355971.html), which makes this year's jump look larger. Mint also said 12.29% is the highest reading in the series that uses 2022-23 as its base year.

**Not every line rose**

- Mineral oils: 45.57%, from 40.02%
- Electricity: 8.06%, after a 0.43% decline in September
- Manufactured products: 9.54%, down from 9.76%
- WPI food index: 8.58%, down from 8.66%

Basic metals rose 17.21% and chemicals 17.53%, [Hindustan Times](https://www.hindustantimes.com/business/wholesale-price-index-wpi-inflation-rises-to-12-29-in-october-amid-sharp-spike-in-fuel-crude-oil-prices-101794813386506.html) and the [Times of India](https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/business/india-business/wholesale-inflation-jumps-to-12-29-in-october-due-to-rising-crude-and-power-prices/articleshow/135876550.cms) reported. The October numbers are provisional, built on an 81.1% response rate, so they can be revised.

**Why rates are in play**

The Reserve Bank of India sets rates to keep retail inflation near a 4% target, with a 2-point band on either side. The [Economic Times](https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/news/economy/indicators/indias-wholesale-inflation-hits-1229-in-october-retail-surpasses-rbis-6-limit/articleshow/135875165.cms) reported that the data has added to expectations of a quarter-point rate rise at the RBI's December meeting.

Bitcoin was near $64,450 at 5:53 a.m. ET, down 1.6% over 24 hours, per CoinGecko.

*In our opinion: a 70.8% jump in crude and gas costs is the load Indian businesses are carrying, and the miss against the Reuters poll was small. The real test comes at the RBI's December meeting, where the Economic Times says a quarter-point rise is now expected. Before then, watch whether retail prices follow wholesale ones, because retail inflation is the gauge the RBI targets.*

articles.title: Japan's Economy Shrinks 0.1% as High Prices Squeeze Shoppers
articles.excerpt: Economists polled by Reuters expected 0.3% growth. Consumer spending fell 0.3% for a second straight quarter, a month before the Bank of Japan meets Dec. 17-18.
articles.body_md:
Japan's economy shrank at an annualized 0.1% in July through September, the Cabinet Office said Monday, its first contraction in four quarters. Economists in a Reuters poll had expected 0.3% growth.

The miss lands a month before the Bank of Japan's Dec. 17-18 policy meeting, and CNBC reported the data could complicate the central bank's plans to keep raising rates.

**Households cut back for a second quarter**

Private consumption, more than half of Japan's output, fell 0.3% from April-June. That is its second straight quarterly drop. Kyodo News pointed to high prices, a magnitude-7.1 earthquake in Kumamoto in late July and heavy August rain, while CNBC reported that household energy subsidies expired in September.

Trade pulled the number down too. Imports rose 2.5% and exports fell 0.2%, so net exports cut 0.6 percentage point from growth, the Cabinet Office tables show. Business investment rose 1.6%.

**Why a tiny drop reads as 0.1%**

The quarter-on-quarter change was small: real GDP slipped 0.02%. "Real" means adjusted for inflation, and in plain yen terms the economy grew 0.4% on the quarter. "Annualized" stretches one quarter's change into the pace it would hit over a full year. The Cabinet Office will revise these figures in a second estimate that folds in fiscal 2025 annual data.

**Economists split on a December hike**

"Today's GDP data is hardly a green light for the BOJ to hike in December," State Street Investment Management economist Krishna Bhimavarapu said in comments reported by CNBC. He pointed to a 2.1% annualized fall in real final sales, a measure of demand that strips out inventories. Capital Economics' Marcel Thieliant still expects a hike, CNBC reported.

Daiwa Institute of Research economist Hirohito Hatanaka told Kyodo that any December hike is unlikely to win a unanimous vote.

Bitcoin was near $64,840 at 11:46 p.m. ET Sunday, up 0.1% over 24 hours, per CoinGecko.

*In our opinion: the 0.1% headline is the small number. The one worth tracking is the 2.1% slide in final sales, because that is the evidence the BOJ board will weigh against inflation on Dec. 18. If the vote splits, the dissents will say more about Japan's next hike than the decision itself.*

articles.title: Fed's Schmid Says Inflation Is 'Moving in the Wrong Direction'
articles.excerpt: The Kansas City Fed chief said the Fed can still cool prices driven by supply shocks or AI spending. He doesn't vote this year, and he didn't call for a hike.
articles.body_md:
Kansas City Fed President Jeff Schmid said on Sunday that inflation is "uncomfortably above the 2% price stability target, and moving in the wrong direction," three weeks before the Fed's Dec. 8-9 meeting.

That matters for anyone holding crypto. Interest-rate futures are fully priced for a quarter-point hike in December, with a small chance of a half-point move, [Reuters reported](https://www.investing.com/news/economy-news/kansas-city-feds-schmid-says-central-bank-has-work-to-do-on-inflation-5028049). Each hike raises what cash and Treasury bills pay, and bitcoin pays nothing by comparison.

**Schmid rejected two explanations for high prices**

Speaking to the National Credit Union Management Association conference in Waikoloa, Hawaii, Schmid disputed the view that repeated supply shocks are to blame. "Demand always plays a role in inflation," he said, per [Reuters](https://www.staradvertiser.com/2026/11/15/breaking-news/still-some-work-to-do-on-inflation-fed-exec-says-at-hawaii-island-meeting/). He also rejected the idea that demand from the artificial intelligence buildout is immune to higher rates.

"Inflation is somehow beyond the Fed's power to control. I don't believe this to be true," he said, describing what both arguments have in common. In prepared remarks, he repeated Chair Kevin Warsh's August line that the Fed has work to do, adding that "our work has only gotten harder since then," [Bloomberg reported](https://news.bloomberglaw.com/banking-law/schmid-says-fed-has-more-work-to-do-to-bring-down-inflation).

**How the rate lever reaches prices**

The Fed sets the federal funds rate, what banks charge each other for overnight loans. Raising it makes borrowing costlier for households and companies, which cools spending. Schmid's point is that this demand channel still works even when an oil shock or a chip shortage is what pushed a price up first.

**What he didn't say**

Schmid did not specifically call for more rate increases, and he isn't a voting member of the Federal Open Market Committee this year, according to [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/15/fed-has-some-work-to-do-on-inflation-kansas-city-fed-chief-says.html). The Fed raised rates a quarter point in September to a 3.75% to 4% range and held in October. Boston Fed President Susan Collins said Saturday she favors a "steady, gradual" path, per [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/15/fed-has-some-work-to-do-on-inflation-kansas-city-fed-chief-says.html).

Bitcoin was near $65,130 at 5:51 p.m. ET, up 2.4% in 24 hours, per [CoinGecko](https://www.coingecko.com/en/coins/bitcoin).

*In our opinion: two regional presidents spent the weekend talking about more tightening, one at a housing conference and one at a credit union meeting in Hawaii, which is a pleasant place to deliver unpleasant news. The phrase to keep is "beyond the Fed's power to control," because Schmid built the whole speech to argue against it. He doesn't vote this year. The officials who do meet Dec. 8-9.*

articles.title: Luxor Says Commander Breach Redirected Clients' Bitcoin Hashrate
articles.excerpt: Just over a dozen client accounts were hit, and Luxor will pay them as if their machines had mined normally. It hasn't said how the attacker got in.
articles.body_md:
Bitcoin mining firm Luxor said on Sunday that someone used its Commander fleet software to point machines in more than 12 client accounts ("just over a dozen," it said) at a different mining pool, and it patched the hole within two hours.

"Every affected client will be paid in full for the redirected hashrate, as if it had mined normally," Luxor said in a statement on X, quoted by [Bitcoin.com News](https://news.bitcoin.com/security/luxor-confirms-bitcoin-mining-hack-and-reveals-ai-enabled-attack/) and [The Defiant](https://thedefiant.io/news/hacks/luxor-pledges-full-compensation-for-commander-hijack). The statement gave no payment date, total amount or method of calculation.

**Why one setting decides the payout**

A mining machine does the work, but a pool address set on each machine decides where that work is credited. The pool then pays rewards to the owner's payout address. Change the pool setting and the machine keeps running at full power while the rewards go to someone else. Luxor's product page says Commander can change pool settings on thousands of miners in one operation, [The Defiant reported](https://cryptonews.net/news/mining/33756034/).

**What Luxor said it fixed**

Luxor said its monitoring caught the redirect overnight, and engineers then began restoring machines to their original pools. The company said Luxor Pool and its LuxOS firmware were not affected and that no data was leaked or taken from its systems. Commander is operating normally, users need to take no action, and a full post-mortem will follow, Luxor said. It gave no date.

**What still isn't known**

Luxor hasn't said how the attacker got in or how many machines were involved. Mining host CoreX Hosting reported about 13 exahashes per second, a measure of computing power, at the address it tied to the attack, according to [The Defiant](https://cryptonews.net/news/mining/33756034/) and [Bitcoin.com News](https://news.bitcoin.com/security/luxor-confirms-bitcoin-mining-hack-and-reveals-ai-enabled-attack/). Luxor hasn't confirmed that figure.

A block found by the OCEAN pool paid about 0.0809 BTC to that address, per on-chain records cited by [CryptoWatchDesk](https://cryptowatchdesk.com/news/security-alert-luxor-confirms-commander-software-breach-ocean-block-paid-attacker-address-0-0809-btc) and [The Defiant](https://cryptonews.net/news/mining/33756034/). OCEAN pays every address with recent work when any pool member finds a block. We found no statement from OCEAN on whether it will act on that payout.

*In our opinion: the weak point here wasn't a pool or a wallet but the dashboard that tells thousands of machines where to send their work. Luxor's pledge covers the clients, but the post-mortem is what other fleet operators need, because it should explain the way in. Until it's published, the 0.0809 BTC sitting at that address is the only payout anyone can see on-chain.*

articles.title: Coinbase Opens a Federal Trust Bank That Can't Take Deposits
articles.excerpt: Custody, not deposits: the OCC wants $60 million of capital and its sign-off before new services. Coinbase's active users fell to 7.4 million last quarter.
articles.body_md:
Coinbase now owns a bank, though not the kind most people picture. Coinbase National Trust Company opened Nov. 9 under a federal charter that lets it hold crypto for clients but not take deposits or make loans, the [OCC's Nov. 6 approval letter](https://www.occ.gov/topics/charters-and-licensing/interpretations-and-decisions/2026/cd1370.pdf) shows.

The business it will take over is large. Coinbase held $376.6 billion of customer crypto and stablecoins on Sept. 30, its [quarterly filing](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1679788/000167978826000122/coin-20260930.htm) shows. Neither the letter nor Coinbase's [Nov. 9 announcement](https://www.coinbase.com/blog/coinbase-launches-national-trust-company-with-federally-regulated-institutional-grade-custody-offering) says how much of that will move into the bank, or when.

**What a trust bank can and can't do**

A national trust bank is a fiduciary: it holds assets for clients and has a legal duty to put their interests first. It takes no insured deposits, so there is no FDIC coverage. Client cash sits in "for benefit of" accounts at other banks, the OCC's April letter says.

For someone who buys bitcoin in the Coinbase app, nothing changes on day one. The charter covers custody "primarily for institutional clients," in the OCC's words.

**Three years of conditions**

For the bank's first three years, the final letter requires:

- At least $60 million of tier 1 capital, with half of it or $30 million, whichever is greater, in cash-like assets
- A separate reserve covering 180 days of operating expenses
- A written OCC non-objection before any significant change, including "any offering of transactional services for custody account customers"

**Who earns what**

Coinbase Custody Trust Company, the New York-chartered firm that serves Coinbase Prime clients today, signed a Sept. 1 agreement to hand those accounts to the bank over time. Staking, Prime Trading and Prime Financing stay with Coinbase affiliates, so their fees land outside the bank. Neither letter lists custody fees.

**Rates, deposits and a market slump**

The Federal Reserve held its target range at 3.75% to 4% on Oct. 28, [its statement](https://www.federalreserve.gov/newsevents/pressreleases/monetary20261028a.htm) shows. Rates reach Coinbase through USDC: lower average rates cut its third-quarter stablecoin revenue by $52.8 million from a year earlier, while bigger USDC balances added $84.6 million, the filing says.

Dollar stablecoin supply fell to $287.05 billion on Saturday, the lowest since September 2025, [DefiLlama](https://defillama.com/stablecoins) data show. The final letter requires the bank to conform, cease or divest activities if needed to meet the GENIUS Act, the 2025 stablecoin law. The April letter says the bank doesn't plan to issue stablecoins.

The slump shows in Coinbase's numbers. Monthly transacting users fell to 7.4 million in the third quarter from 9.3 million a year earlier. Bitcoin was near $64,970 at 3:47 p.m. ET Sunday, per [CoinGecko](https://www.coingecko.com/en/coins/bitcoin), after dipping below $63,000 on Saturday night.

**Who else holds one, and who objects**

Anchorage Digital got there first. It won OCC approval on Jan. 13, 2021, and [calls itself](https://www.anchorage.com/press-room/introducing-anchorage-digital-bank-the-first-federally-chartered-digital-asset-bank) the first federally chartered digital asset bank. On Dec. 12, 2025, the OCC [conditionally approved](https://www.occ.gov/news-issuances/news-releases/2025/nr-occ-2025-125.html) [Circle's](https://www.occ.gov/topics/charters-and-licensing/interpretations-and-decisions/2026/ca1356.pdf) First National Digital Currency Bank, Ripple, BitGo, Fidelity Digital Assets and Paxos. Ripple [won final approval](https://ripple.com/ripple-press/ripple-receives-final-occ-approval-to-establish-national-trust-bank/) on Oct. 26.

The Independent Community Bankers of America [sued the OCC](https://www.icba.org/w/occ-release-oct-2026) on Oct. 2, [Reuters reported](https://www.reuters.com/world/community-banks-sue-us-regulator-over-crypto-firm-charters-2026-10-02/), challenging its March chartering rule and Protego Holdings' approval. "Congress did not create the national trust charter as a side door into the banking system for crypto firms," ICBA chief Rebeca Romero Rainey said. The OCC wrote in April that it "has the capability to resolve an uninsured national bank." Rick Schonberg, the bank's CEO, wrote in Coinbase's Nov. 9 post: "Custody is foundational to our business."

*In our opinion: "bank" is accurate, but the letter describes a custodian on a three-year leash. Its first test arrives in a weak market, with fewer active users and a stablecoin business tied to Fed rates. The number to follow is how much of the $376.6 billion moves into the bank, and Coinbase hasn't published a schedule. The ICBA case matters too, since a ruling against the March rule would reach every crypto trust bank the OCC has approved.*

articles.title: Coinone Says Support Contractor Breach Exposed Customer ID Numbers
articles.excerpt: Passwords, bank details and national ID numbers shared with Coinone's help desk may have leaked. The exchange says its trading and wallet systems were separate.
articles.body_md:
Coinone customers who used the South Korean exchange's help desk may have had passwords, bank account numbers and national ID numbers exposed, the exchange said in a notice posted at 6 p.m. ET Saturday. The breach hit MetaM, the outside firm that runs its customer support.

An attacker got into MetaM's servers around 2 p.m. ET on Nov. 11 (4 a.m. Nov. 12 in Seoul) and viewed or took stored support records, [Coinone's notice](https://coinone.co.kr/info/notice/5950) says. Customers who never used chat or phone support are not affected.

**What sat in the support logs**

A support log holds whatever a customer typed or said to an agent. Coinone's list of items at risk: phone number, name, email, birth date, bank account, password, resident registration number (South Korea's national ID), ID issue date, home address, wallet address and transaction ID. The leaked items differ by conversation. Coinone said it plans a lookup service so each customer can check.

How many people are affected? The notice doesn't say, and [The Asia Business Daily](https://www.asiae.co.kr/en/article/2026111511161281774) and [ChosunBiz](https://biz.chosun.com/en/en-finance/2026/11/15/37SXPOUOARCZLIE2N7NORVPNDU/) reports give no count.

**Trading and wallet systems run apart**

Coinone said its accounts, trading and wallet systems are separate from MetaM's servers and show no sign of intrusion. Every login needs a second check (an OTP code or KakaoTalk verification on the owner's phone), so the leaked details alone can't be used to log in or withdraw, the exchange said.

It moved outsourced support to email only and reported the incident to the Korea Internet & Security Agency, the Personal Information Protection Commission and the Financial Supervisory Service. MetaM said in its own Nov. 14 notice that not every user's data leaked, [Yonhap](https://www.yna.co.kr/view/AKR20261114049400017) reported.

**What Coinone asked customers to do**

Anyone who shared a password with support should change it there and anywhere it's reused, Coinone said. It never asks for passwords, OTP numbers or verification codes, or for withdrawals, by phone, text or email. Under Korean privacy law, customers who can't prove an exact loss can seek statutory damages of up to 3 million won, the notice says.

*In our opinion: the leak came through a help desk, and the risk now is impersonation. The notice still leaves out the number of people in the leaked logs and the date its lookup service opens. Until then, a call citing an old support chat deserves suspicion, as Coinone itself warned.*

articles.title: Bitcoin Climbs 5% Off Four-Month Low as Fear Gauge Hits 10
articles.excerpt: Bitcoin is still down about 14% on the week near $65,500. Ether bounced 6.6% from $1,711, its weakest level since July 8.
articles.body_md:
Bitcoin climbed about 5.4% from its Saturday-night low to near $65,500 at 5:52 a.m. ET Sunday, [CoinGecko](https://www.coingecko.com/en/coins/bitcoin) data show. The bounce came as a widely watched sentiment gauge sat at 10 out of 100.

The low came at about 8:45 p.m. ET Saturday, near $62,120 on CoinGecko's five-minute data. [The Straits Times](https://www.straitstimes.com/business/binance-targets-full-reopening-of-withdrawals-by-next-week1), carrying Reuters and Bloomberg reporting, put the bottom at $62,112, bitcoin's weakest since July 14. Even after the rebound, bitcoin is down 13.9% over seven days and 2.6% over 24 hours.

**Ether's low reached back to July**

Ether fell as far as $1,711, its lowest since July 8, according to the same report. CoinGecko had it near $1,828 at 5:52 a.m., up 6.6% from its low but down 18.6% on the week. Solana traded near $71.89, down 19.6% over seven days.

**What the fear gauge measures**

The [Crypto Fear & Greed Index](https://alternative.me/crypto/fear-and-greed-index/) from Alternative.me scores bitcoin sentiment from 0, "Extreme Fear," to 100, "Extreme Greed." It mixes price swings and drawdowns (25%), trading volume and momentum (25%), social media activity (15%), bitcoin's share of the crypto market (10%) and search trends (10%). Its survey piece is paused. Sunday's reading of 10 was the lowest since June 9, when it hit 9. A week earlier it stood at 29.

**Money has been leaving the funds**

U.S. spot bitcoin ETFs saw almost $3 billion of net outflows from Oct. 30 through Nov. 13, The Straits Times reported. [Farside Investors](https://farside.co.uk/btc/) data show $185.4 million left on Friday alone. Bitcoin has fallen about 25% since Oct. 21.

Richard Galvin, executive chairman at crypto investment firm DACM, said Anthropic's upcoming initial public offering may be drawing money away from crypto. "It appears crypto remains a short-term funding source, particularly for retail investors," he said in the report.

*In our opinion: the number that matters this week is the ETF tally on Monday, the first trading day after the bounce. Five percent back is a modest recovery inside a 25% slide since late October. The gauge last read this low in early June, and its next update lands around 7 p.m. ET Sunday.*

articles.title: Stablecoin Supply Falls to $287 Billion, Lowest Since September 2025
articles.excerpt: USDT shrank by $8.17 billion in 30 days and USDC by $3.53 billion as redemptions outpaced new issuance, DefiLlama data show.
articles.body_md:
The supply of dollar stablecoins fell on 13 of the 14 days through Saturday, to $287.05 billion, its lowest level since September 2025, [DefiLlama](https://defillama.com/stablecoins) data show.

That is $25.8 billion, or 8.2%, below the May 17 peak of $312.85 billion. About $9.3 billion of it has left since Nov. 1, and $4.4 billion in the past seven days.

**Tether accounts for most of the drop**

USDT, the largest stablecoin, shrank by $8.17 billion over 30 days to $175.36 billion on DefiLlama's count. Tether's own [transparency page](https://tether.to/en/transparency/) lists $175.4 billion of liabilities and $180.9 billion of assets, a cushion of about $5.5 billion.

USDC fell $3.53 billion over the same 30 days to $69.3 billion. Circle's [USDC page](https://www.circle.com/usdc) shows a lower figure, 67.9 billion USDC in circulation as of Nov. 12. The page doesn't explain the gap, and DefiLlama's tally adds up tokens across many blockchains.

**How a stablecoin shrinks**

A stablecoin is a token built to stay worth $1. Circle says businesses with a Circle Mint account send it dollars and receive the same amount of new USDC, which it calls minting. When they hand USDC back for dollars, the tokens are burned and leave circulation.

So supply only falls when more tokens are redeemed than created. Each redemption pays dollars out of the issuer's reserves. Mint accounts are open to exchanges, banks and large trading firms, not to individuals, according to Circle.

Not every token dropped: Ripple's RLUSD grew $390 million over 30 days, to $2.8 billion, DefiLlama shows.

The decline has come alongside a slide in crypto prices. Bitcoin was near $64,990 at 11:55 p.m. ET Saturday, down 3.1% in 24 hours, per [CoinGecko](https://www.coingecko.com/en/coins/bitcoin).

*In our opinion: the number to follow is USDT. It made up about $8.2 billion of the past month's decline, more than twice USDC's share, while Tether's page still shows assets above what it owes. The latest daily reading was flat, so the next few DefiLlama prints will show whether the redemptions have paused or only taken Saturday off.*

articles.title: Bitcoin Falls to $62,500 as Exchanges Force Out Leveraged Longs
articles.excerpt: Seven exchanges force-closed $1.29 billion of futures in 24 hours, 94% of them longs, Swolecharts data shows. Binance accounted for $727 million.
articles.body_md:
Bitcoin fell as low as $62,534 on Coinbase by 8:19 p.m. ET Saturday, as exchanges force-closed more than $1.2 billion of long futures bets in 24 hours.

CoinGecko showed bitcoin near $62,810 at that time, down 7.9% in 24 hours and about 16% over seven days. Kraken's low was $62,540.

**Longs took almost all of it**

[Swolecharts](https://swolecharts.com/liquidations) recorded $1.29 billion of forced closures in the 24 hours to 8:19 p.m. ET, on seven exchanges. Long positions, bets that prices would rise, accounted for $1.21 billion, or 94%, across 239,754 liquidations. Bitcoin contracts made up $487.9 million, ether $386.2 million and Solana $72.0 million. Binance led at $727.2 million, ahead of Bybit and Gate. The largest single order was a $16.17 million ether long on Binance.

Swolecharts calls the totals a lower bound, because Binance publishes only a sample when trading is busy. [Crypto Briefing](https://cryptobriefing.com/crypto-market-liquidations-bitcoin-slide/), citing CoinGlass at 7:17 p.m. ET, put the 24-hour total at $1.9 billion, $1.8 billion of it longs. [ChainCatcher](https://www.chaincatcher.com/en/article/2304823), also citing CoinGlass, gave $1.945 billion, 318,286 traders and the same $16.17 million Binance ether-USDT order.

**How a forced close works**

Many futures traders put down only part of a position's value, called leverage. If losses eat through that deposit, the exchange closes the trade and sells it. That forced sale is a liquidation. It can push the price into the next group of trigger points.

**Ether, XRP and the other large coins**

Smaller coins fell harder. Prices at 8:19 p.m. ET, per CoinGecko, with 24-hour and seven-day changes. Coinbase and Kraken showed the same direction:

- Ether: about $1,731, down 10.2% and 22%
- XRP: about $0.917, down 8.9% and 21%
- Solana: about $69.11, down 10.7% and 23%
- BNB: about $572, down 9.2% and 17%
- Dogecoin: about $0.0564, down 12.5% and 21%
- Cardano: about $0.145, down 13.2% and 19%

U.S. spot bitcoin ETFs posted $185.4 million of net outflows Friday, a seventh straight session and about $1.91 billion since Nov. 5, [Farside Investors](https://farside.co.uk/btc/) data shows, matching the SoSoValue figure in a [Yahoo Finance report](https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/crypto/articles/bitcoin-slides-below-68-000-061956476.html). [Black Mint reported Friday](https://blackmint.markets/news/bitcoin-weekly-drop-nasdaq-best-week/) that bitcoin ended the week near $68,400.

*In our opinion: the closures hit traders still long on borrowed money as the price dropped into the $62,000s. Swolecharts and CoinGlass cover different venues, but both show longs taking more than 90% of the forced sales. The funds do not trade again until Monday.*

articles.title: XRP Sinks to One-Year Low as Altcoins Fall Harder Than Bitcoin
articles.excerpt: Bitcoin slipped under $64,000 Saturday evening, down 6.7% in a day. Cardano, Solana and Uniswap's UNI each fell more than 11%, per CoinGecko.
articles.body_md:
XRP fell to about $0.902 at 5:48 p.m. ET on Saturday, down 10.6% in 24 hours, per [CoinGecko](https://www.coingecko.com/en/coins/xrp). That is the lowest daily reading in CoinGecko's XRP data for the past year, and about 22% below the $1.16 it fetched on Nov. 8.

The rest of the market slid with it. The total value of all crypto fell about 9% in a day to roughly $2.18 trillion, CoinGecko data shows.

[Black Mint reported at noon](https://blackmint.markets/news/bitcoin-lowest-since-august-etf-outflows/) that bitcoin had hit its lowest level since August, near $65,380. By evening it was lower still.

**Smaller coins took the bigger hits**

Prices at 5:48 p.m. ET and 24-hour changes, per CoinGecko:

- Bitcoin: about $63,760, down 6.7%, its lowest daily reading since Aug. 17
- Ether: about $1,758, down 8.8%, its lowest since July 10
- Solana: about $69.48, down 11.2%
- Cardano: about $0.1456, down 13.1%
- Uniswap's UNI: about $4.75, down 17.2%

**How forced selling feeds a slide**

Many traders hold crypto futures bought partly with borrowed money, which is called leverage. If prices fall far enough that a trader's deposit no longer covers the loss, the exchange closes the position and sells, a step called liquidation. Those sales can push prices down to the next group of trigger points.

An [Investing.com report carried by Yahoo Finance](https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/crypto/articles/bitcoin-slides-below-68-000-061956476.html) tied Saturday's losses to forced liquidations, a week of outflows from U.S. spot bitcoin ETFs and a broader pullback from tech and AI stocks. It said bitcoin was headed for a sixth straight weekly loss and was down more than 20% since Oct. 21.

[The Crypto Times](https://www.cryptotimes.io/2026/11/14/xrp-price-falls-below-1-to-lowest-since-august-as-analyst-warns-of-0-80-drop/) said XRP's drop appeared to come from market-wide pressure rather than news about XRP itself.

*In our opinion: the detail worth noticing is the order of the damage. Bitcoin fell 6.7%, ether 8.8% and several large altcoins by double digits, which is how a market sheds risk from the edges inward. XRP has now given back about a fifth of its value in six days. The first real test of demand comes Monday, when the ETFs open again after a weekend of trading without them.*

articles.title: Fed's Collins Backs 'Steady, Gradual' Hikes Ahead of Dec. 8-9 Meeting
articles.excerpt: The Boston Fed chief said recent price data and a firmer job market mean rates over the next year could end up 'a bit higher' than she thought.
articles.body_md:
Boston Fed President Susan Collins said on Saturday she favors modest rate increases taken one small step at a time, with the Fed's target range at 3.75% to 4% and its next decision due Dec. 8-9.

"A steady, gradual path seems appropriate to me at the moment. But I'm open-minded," Collins told reporters at a Boston Fed housing conference, [Reuters reported](https://www.investing.com/news/economy-news/feds-collins-says-gradual-rate-hikes-best-to-manage-economic-risks-5027385).

For crypto holders, the Fed's pace sets the return on cash. Each hike raises what Treasury bills and money-market funds pay, and bitcoin pays nothing by comparison.

**Why she argued against a faster pace**

Collins said she sees the risks as two-sided. Inflation is high and spreading through the economy, she said, while the job market is stable with room to speed up. She also said the rise in longer-term borrowing costs this year could weigh on demand more than she expects. Taken together, she said, that argues against speeding up, according to [Reuters](https://www.investing.com/news/economy-news/feds-collins-says-gradual-rate-hikes-best-to-manage-economic-risks-5027385) and [Investing.com](https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/feds-collins-backs-gradual-rate-hikes-sees-inflation-and-jobs-risks-as-twosided-5027401).

She added that gradual "doesn't necessarily mean a particular cadence," and that price data from the past three months has pushed her expected rate path for the next year "a bit higher" than she thought a couple of months ago.

**How a hike works**

The federal funds rate is what banks charge each other for overnight loans. A quarter-point increase in December would lift the range to 4% to 4.25%. Reuters reported the Fed last raised rates in September, and that markets expect quarter-point moves in December and again in January. Bloomberg, cited by [Finansavisen](https://www.finansavisen.no/makro/2026/11/14/8395858/fed-topp-bor-heve-renten-jevnt-og-gradvis), reported that market pricing points to one more hike in March or April.

Not every official agrees on size. Reuters said Fed Governor Christopher Waller's recent comments raised expectations that some officials want a bigger move next month.

Bitcoin was near $63,760 at 5:48 p.m. ET, down 6.7% in 24 hours, per [CoinGecko](https://www.coingecko.com/en/coins/bitcoin).

*In our opinion: the real argument inside the Fed is no longer whether to hike, but by how much. Collins wants small steps; Waller's remarks pointed the other way. With inflation above the 2% target for more than five years, per Reuters, the Dec. 8-9 statement is where that debate gets settled, at least until January.*

articles.title: BoE's Greene Calls Waiting on Inflation the 'Bigger Policy Mistake'
articles.excerpt: The Bank of England lifted rates to 4% this month and expects inflation near 5% by mid-2027. Its next decision is due Dec. 17.
articles.body_md:
Bank of England policymaker Megan Greene said on Saturday it is less risky to raise rates too far and cut later than to wait, with Bank Rate at 4% after this month's hike from 3.75%.

"The risk of not getting on top of inflation coming out of a period when we've had inflation over target for the best part of about five-and-a-half years, that's the bigger risk, that would be the bigger policy mistake," Greene told a Centre for European Reform conference in London, [Reuters reported](https://live.euronext.com/en/financial-news/boes-greene-says-acting-proactively-now-inflation-would-screw-things-least).

Her worry is the second round. Greene wrote earlier this week that the bank should "proactively tighten" to guard against pay growth getting stuck around 3.5% or higher and firms passing those costs on, according to Reuters and [PiQ Markets](https://piqmarkets.com/story/boe-s-greene-says-acting-early-on-inflation-limits-policy-error).

**What a second-round effect is**

A first-round effect is a direct price jump, such as higher energy bills. The second round comes when workers win bigger raises to keep up and companies lift prices to cover the wages, which can keep inflation high after the original shock fades. The Bank of England's own [rate page](https://www.bankofengland.co.uk/monetary-policy/the-interest-rate-bank-rate) says energy prices have stayed high because of conflict in the Middle East, puts inflation at 3.5% against a 2% target, and says it expects inflation to reach about 5% by mid-2027.

Greene voted with the majority for the November hike and earlier sat in a minority that wanted to move sooner, Reuters reported.

**More hikes priced in**

Markets are betting on another Bank of England increase in December and two or possibly three more quarter-point moves in 2027, per Reuters. Chief Economist Huw Pill told the Financial Times in an interview published Saturday that further increases are likely to be needed in 2027 beyond December, Reuters said.

For crypto, the link runs through yields. When central banks lift rates, cash and government bonds pay more, which raises the bar for assets that pay no interest, bitcoin included. The Fed decides on Dec. 8-9 and the Bank of England on Dec. 17.

articles.excerpt: U.S. spot bitcoin ETFs lost money in all five sessions last week, led by BlackRock's IBIT at $908 million. A fear gauge fell to 13 of 100.
articles.body_md:
Bitcoin fell to about $65,380 at 11:58 a.m. ET on Saturday, down 4.7% in 24 hours, per [CoinGecko](https://www.coingecko.com/en/coins/bitcoin). That is its lowest daily reading in CoinGecko's data since Aug. 19, when it closed near $64,690.

The slide extends a rough week. Bitcoin sat near $75,780 on Nov. 8, so Saturday's price is about 13.7% lower, and its market value is down to roughly $1.31 trillion.

**Five straight days of ETF outflows**

U.S. spot bitcoin ETFs posted net outflows in every session from Nov. 9 through Nov. 13, about $1.07 billion in total, according to [Farside Investors](https://farside.co.uk/btc/) data:

- Monday: $201.0 million out
- Tuesday: $95.0 million
- Wednesday: $299.8 million
- Thursday: $284.1 million
- Friday: $185.4 million

BlackRock's IBIT accounted for about $908 million of that. Fidelity's FBTC lost $41.9 million on Friday alone. (Source: Farside Investors.)

**How a redemption reaches the market**

A spot bitcoin ETF holds actual bitcoin. When more shares are cashed in than created, the fund's authorized participants (the big trading firms that swap shares with the fund) hand shares back and the fund releases bitcoin or sells it for cash. So a week of outflows means less bitcoin held for brokerage-account investors. It is one of the few daily, public measures of that demand. Weekend prices move with no ETF trading at all, because the funds only trade Monday to Friday.

Sentiment followed the price. [Alternative.me's Crypto Fear & Greed Index](https://alternative.me/crypto/fear-and-greed-index/), a 0-100 gauge where lower means more fear, read 13 on Saturday, down from 20 a day earlier. Ether fared worse, falling 5.3% to about $1,826, per [CoinGecko](https://www.coingecko.com/en/coins/ethereum).

No single headline explains Saturday's leg down.

*In our opinion: the number to track is Monday's ETF tally. Five red sessions took about $1.07 billion out, yet Farside still shows the funds roughly $54.7 billion ahead in net inflows since launch; last week's exits equal about 2% of that total. Bitcoin doesn't keep banker's hours, though, and Saturday's drop came with every one of those funds closed.*
